utterances.text: Witness, the police station in Samac would have been restructured, as you put it. Even had these men not arrived, were there enough local forces to perform the tasks set by the SDS without any difficulty?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no difficulty. It could have been Obudovac on its own. It could have accomplished the task.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djukic, were there any civilian casualties as Samac was taken over between the 16th and the 17th?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I would say that it was a large-scale raid rather than a war.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djukic, my learned friend, Ms. Marcus, gave you a document to read over the break, which is P1418. Did you review the document?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I wanted to be told if it was Milan Milicic who signed the document, because if that is the case then I can tell you that I know this document by heart from my previous time as officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Then, if you know, tell us, who is behind the document? Who inspired the document?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The discontented Simo Zaric who was convicted here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know why Simo Zaric inspired certain individuals to draw up this document?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he had the ambition to become the president of the republic, and he was an Orthodox communist.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we have a look at P1418, the last page in both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you tell us the following. Do you know if Mile Beronja who signed this, a colonel, was involved in crime in Samac in 1992?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, whether that was the case or not, he got involved with a woman, and because of him we weren't able to liberate the villages of Bukvik and another one. And we had our people, Serbs, who were stranded there. He was a very poor officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djukic, can you please have a look at the list of signatories here. Tell us, if you know, whether any of these individuals were involved in criminal activities in Samac in 1992?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in Samac they were not. However, Captain Milan Josic, an elite captain of a battalion, was killed on account of crime. He was killed in a traffic accident or at least something that was engineered to look like that. And there was also something about Jovan Erletic. Another thing, it is quite odd that Simo Zaric should be writing this, as a school's officer [as interpreted], that somebody was killed and that he should not file a criminal report about it. The military prosecutor Gajic was one that would be bringing charges against suspected perpetrators. It was stated here that he was killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what it was that Simo Zaric wanted to achieve with this document?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A career. He wanted a promotion. Other -- otherwise, he was a singer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djukic, can you clarify this. Let's move to Brcko. At the point of the takeover of power in Brcko, when was it that Zika Crnogorac, the person that we talked about, showed up?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only after the commander of the Bijeljina Guard, Savic, aka Mauzer, moved on to take up some other duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Really slow down, slightly. Adjusting our speed of speech takes more time than to reduce the speed with 15 per cent. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djukic, was it before or after the takeover or liberation of Brcko?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: You told us, and this perhaps remained unclear after your today's evidence, was Zika Crnogorac a criminal himself, or was he the person who went about arresting criminals in Brcko in December of 1992 -- in the summer of 1992?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, according to what he was doing, he was indeed trying to prevent crime, and that's something I heard from others. But he also went about abusing individuals, extorting statements from them. And you misunderstood me. He didn't take all of the vehicles to Pale. Some of the vehicles had gone missing before. He only said that he took several vehicles and some valuables to Pale to Karadzic, which isn't something that I saw myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Let's take it bit by bit, Witness. First, the mistreatment of those who were arrested, of which ethnicity were they and what was he trying to do?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were Serbs, all of them. Some of them were even active duty policemen and inspectors of the SUP. He was forcing admissions out of them, confessions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Second, Mr. Djukic, he went about arresting perpetrators of crime based on these very statements that he forced out of those other people. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Next, he tried to find perpetrators of the theft of vehicles; right?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He took up files relating to certain BMWs that were already missing, but there were records of these vehicles and he was trying to find their whereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And the reason why he was trying to find where they were was because they -- he wanted to find out who the perpetrators were.

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because they were vehicles belonging to Muslims. And it was proper that these vehicles be returned to them because there were quite a few Muslims living in our area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. One second. Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I understand the time constraints, but the leading questions are truly piling up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. To some extent, of course, they are in response to question put by others, to say so. Mr. Petrovic, I would have another concern apart from the leading character of the questions; that is, often this type of quick gaining of information lacks entirely the basis on which the witness is able to testify. Please proceed. You've got three minutes left.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djukic, what is the basis or the source of your knowledge about Zika Crnogorac and his attempts to enforce at least some appearance of law and order in Brcko?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said yesterday that Boro and Petar Kaurinovic, colleagues of mine, attended studies part-time in Zagreb. They were the ones who provided me with this information as colleagues more than anything else, and they asked me to advise them as to what they should do so -- so that they would not exceed their powers conferred upon them by the law.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: These two individuals you mentioned, were they in any way connected to Zika Crnogorac?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They provided him with information not because they wanted to but because there were certain inhabitants of Brcko who were the untouchables, the protected ones, and I have to mention, of course, that they were in the SUP, and they were working on crimes. And they did file criminal reports for all these cases. None of them were left behind in drawers.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we look at P3038, page 15 in English and 13 in B/C/S. Have a look at the document. Specifically the left-hand side. Is there anywhere in this document that it is indicated that it was produced in the State Security Department of the Republic of Serbia, or that it had to do with the reserve force of the State Security Services? Does this in any way indicate any sort of link between this individual and the State Security Service?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am a bit puzzled by what is written there, "I," or "on behalf of the Department of Serbia." This isn't quite legible --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the witness repeat what he said.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours. Misleading. The question is misleading. I wouldn't want to say why it's misleading, but I think Mr. Petrovic understands why. The document is a part of a file. That is what I said in the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And that makes also what is not found in a document, Mr. Petrovic, is easy to establish by two intelligent or three intelligent parties to look at the document than to find that no reference is made to food, for example. Of course, that's obvious. Whether there's any other reason -- I mean, what this witness says about that he doesn't find anything in this document. That doesn't help us in any way, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I agree fully. And I am -- I wonder why my learned friend showed this document to the witness in order to establish that there was a link with state security, because it is a quite apparent that it cannot be established on -- on this basis. That's why I showed the document to the witness again. I have one more question left, with your leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djukic, was it the case that in the MUP that the MUP would admit anyone with a criminal record, anyone with criminal convictions based on your knowledge and experience stemming from your police career?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Article 45 of the Law on the MUP of the Republic of Serbia, as well as of other republics, clearly stated that such an individual could be admitted only if it had to do with a traffic accident, which was done -- committed out of negligence, but it could not involve in any case a property crime or a crime in general.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Djukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I promised you, Ms. Marcus, if there was any time left, I would give it to you. Also in view of the fact that the two Defence teams, to a large extent, also for the Stanisic Defence in cross-examination, seeking evidence on its own case, there was close to six hours, where you had three half hours. One question. Let's see how much time that takes, and then we'll see whether there's time for the second one.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I withdraw the question, Your Honour [overlapping speakers].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Both?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes [Overlapping speakers]. Thank you, Mr. Djukic. Both.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Djukic, since the Judges have no further questions for you, this concludes your evidence. You may remain seated. Mr. Djukic, I'd like to thank you for coming to The Hague. I'm glad that your medical condition was such that you could give your evidence these days. You've answered the questions put to you by the parties, by the Bench. Thank you for that. And I wish you a safe return home again. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. And I apologise, once again, for speaking too fast.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At least those words were spoken in the appropriate pace. Everyone will be happy with these last words. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We adjourn for the day, and we will resume Tuesday, the 13th of March, quarter past 2.00 in this same courtroom, II. We stand adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 13th day of March, 2012, at 2.15 p.m. 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.13 p.m.,
